strongest_objection: The event lacks a confirmed end time and the rain gauges are >5 km from the outfall; such spacing can easily miss localized rain, while sensor or data‑feed glitches can produce a prolonged open signal, making the dry‑spill inference unreliable.

case.summary: Storm overflow SBB00211 (South West Water) discharging to the Carnon River began spilling at 2026-11-13 17:14:21 UTC. There is no recorded end time and the status is null, so the event was still open-ended at 21.1 hours when the data was pulled. The monitor is reported online (monitor_offline: false). Two Environment Agency rain gauges were checked. Station 48182 (5.7 km away) recorded 0.0 mm in the 24h before the spill, 0.0 mm in the 24-48h before, and 0.0 mm during the spill. Station 48103 (6.5 km away) recorded 0.2 mm in the 24h before, 0.0 mm in the 24-48h before, and 0.0 mm during. Across both gauges the maximum was 0.2 mm in the preceding 48 hours and 0.0 mm during a discharge of more than 21 hours. That is far too little rain to plausibly explain a storm discharge, and the feed flags it as a 'dry_spill_candidate'. This points to a possible permit breach (discharge without heavy rainfall), but it is not conclusive. Both gauges are more than 5 km from the outfall, so localised rain could have been missed, and the event record is unclosed. The two memory entries are earlier reviews of this same event, not separate prior spills. Those reviews reached 'likely_innocent' (confidence 0.35) and 'needs_review' (confidence 0.55), neither with any external sources (n_sources: 0). One prior objection said both gauges recorded zero rain in the preceding 48h; in fact station 48103 recorded 0.2 mm in the 0-24h window. That figure is still negligible.
breach_indicators: Maximum rainfall during the spill was 0.0 mm at both gauges (48182 at 5.7 km, 48103 at 6.5 km).
Maximum rainfall in the 24h before the spill was only 0.2 mm (station 48103); station 48182 recorded 0.0 mm.
Maximum rainfall 24-48h before the spill was 0.0 mm at both gauges, so antecedent wet conditions are not evident from these gauges.
Discharge duration was 21.1 hours with no recorded end time, suggesting a prolonged, possibly ongoing release in dry conditions.
The monitor is reported online (monitor_offline: false), so the discharge signal is not obviously a monitor-offline artefact.
The automated verdict from the joined feed is 'dry_spill_candidate'.
Two independent gauges in different locations agree on near-zero rainfall.
questions_for_evidence: Does Met Office or Environment Agency rainfall radar for 2026-11-11 to 2026-11-14 show any localised rain over the Carnon River catchment upstream of the outfall (approx. 50.2185, -5.1038) that the gauges 5.7-6.5 km away could have missed?
Are there any rain gauges or weather stations closer to the outfall than 5.7 km with readings for 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-14?
What is the final status and end time of event SBB00211 starting 2026-11-13 17:14:21 in South West Water's live storm overflow map or EDM data, and what was the true total duration?
Did South West Water report any operational cause for this spill, such as a pump failure, power outage, blockage or emergency overflow, which would indicate a non-rainfall discharge?
Is there evidence of high groundwater or infiltration in the area in November 2026 that the company might cite as a cause? This would need checking against the near-zero 48h rainfall.
What does the EA-issued permit for overflow SBB00211 say, including any pass-forward flow conditions and the conditions under which spills are permitted?
Have the Environment Agency, Surfers Against Sewage or local groups (e.g. around Restronguet Creek/Carnon River) reported pollution or sewage observations around 13-14 November 2026?
Has this overflow recorded other dry-weather spill events on separate dates in South West Water's annual EDM returns, which would establish a genuine pattern?
Did tidal conditions or tide-locking affect the outfall on 13-14 November 2026, which could explain a discharge unrelated to rainfall?

evidence.report:
# Evidence pack: SBB00211, South West Water, Carnon River (event start 2026-11-13 17:14 UTC)

**Bottom line:** I found nothing online that clears this event, and nothing that confirms it as a breach. The case still rests on the gauge data. The dry-weather context is consistent with the gauges. I found no reported pump failure or other operational cause, but that doesn't prove there wasn't one. The open questions can only be answered with records from South West Water or the Environment Agency (EA). The searches did not turn up those records.

I ran 5 searches. Every fact below is cited. Where I found nothing, I say so.

## 1. What supports a breach

- **Region-wide dry conditions.** On 5 Nov 2026, regulators said parts of the area South West Water serves "remain in severe drought" (https://manyangles.news/story/2026-11-05/south-west-waters-failure-to-fix-leaks-putting-customer-bopxq3; https://dailydigest.com/story/south-west-waters-failure-to-fix-leaks-putting-customer-supplies-at-risk-457072/). Devon County Council referred to "the dry weather" (https://www.devon.gov.uk/news/devon-county-council-statement-letter-regulators-revealing-south-west-waters-leakage-record-getting-worse-putting-supplies-risk-despite-being-warned-seven-successive-years/). This fits the near-zero gauge readings, but the sources don't say whether the drought covers the Carnon catchment.
- **Weak local weather hint.** An events listing for Truro (about 5 km north) showed "5°C · 0% rain" for 12 Nov 2026 (https://eventslist.co.uk/truro/events/the-us-office-trivia-at-mason-brewing-co-2026-11-12). This is a forecast widget, not a measurement, and it covers the day before the spill.
- **The company's record.** On 29 Sep 2026, South West Water was fined £7,867,733 plus £329,993 costs after pleading guilty to 18 EA charges for 2015–2021. Seventeen were illegal discharges, and one was failing to take remedial measures after a pumping-station failure (https://theintelligent.co.uk/environment/2026/south-west-water-fined-nearly-ps8-million-sewage-spills-across-devon-and-cornwall; https://www.cmscoms.com/south-west-water-guilty-of-six-years-of-illegal-sewage-discharges/). One of the sites was **Playing Place**, a village close to the Carnon catchment.
  - **Caveat:** I can't confirm that any charged asset is SBB00211. The company said most charges "concerned the use of overflows in storm conditions" (https://www.thepost.uk.com/news/courts/south-west-water-hit-with-ps8-million-fine-for-sewage-pollution-959435). The case is not evidence of dry-weather spilling at this site.
- **The "dry spill" threshold.** Reporting describes dry spills as discharges when rainfall is below 0.25 mm (summary returned by the search at https://theintelligent.co.uk/environment/2026/south-west-water-fined-nearly-ps8-million-sewage-spills-across-devon-and-cornwall). Every window in the gauge data is at or below 0.2 mm, which is under that threshold. The cited page doesn't state this definition explicitly, so check it before relying on it.
- **Wider pattern.** Suspected dry-weather discharges reportedly rose sharply in early 2026 (https://lalumierecollective.com/article/water-companies-dry-weather-sewage-discharges-skyrocket-is-our-environment-at-risk). This is a low-quality aggregator and is background only.

## 2. Testing the innocent explanations

- **Pump failure or power outage (the skeptic rated this "high"):** I found **no report** of a pumping-station failure or power cut at Devoran, Bissoe or Carnon Downs in Nov 2026. The search turned up only leakage and drought stories. This doesn't rule out a failure, because these are often not publicised. It also matters legally: the 2026 prosecution shows a pump failure can be an offence in itself (failing to take remedial measures), not automatically an excuse.
- **Localised rain the gauges missed:** I found **no weather report** of rain at Truro or the Carnon area on 13–14 Nov 2026. The search returned only US forecasts. This remains a theoretical objection with nothing supporting it.
- **Pollution in the river from another source:** The Carnon River and Restronguet Creek are well known for **mine-water pollution**, including the 1992 Wheal Jane release and ongoing metal contamination (https://challenginghabitat.com/2023/10/17/restronguet-creek-revisited/; https://www.feockparishcouncil.gov.uk/ourcreek). That matters if anyone uses river colour or water quality as evidence, but it doesn't explain a signal from a sewage overflow monitor.
- **Tide-locking:** Restronguet Creek is the tidal part of the river (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restronguet_Creek; https://www.feockparishcouncil.gov.uk/ourcreek). That makes tidal effects physically possible if the outfall is in or near the tidal reach. I have no evidence that it is.
- **Monitor fault or a record that never closed:** I found nothing either way.

## 3. Still unknown (needs requests to the company or the EA)

- The final end time, status and total duration of the event from South West Water's live storm overflow map or monitoring data.
- Any operational cause the company records (pump, power, blockage).
- Rainfall radar for 11–14 Nov, and any gauge closer than 5.7 km.
- The permit conditions for SBB00211, including how much flow must pass to treatment before it may spill.
- Whether SBB00211 is linked to the Playing Place charges.
- Earlier dry-day spills from this overflow on other dates.
- Tide times and whether the outfall sits in the tidal reach.
- Groundwater levels.
- Any public pollution reports from 13–14 Nov. I found none.

**Assessment:** The dry-weather background makes the rain-gauge evidence stronger. The skeptic's "high" rating for a pump failure is a hypothesis with no evidence behind it, and even a pump failure could itself be an offence. The skeptic's 0.25 breach confidence seems low, but this still falls short of conclusive. Treat it as a **credible dry-spill candidate**, and get the company's monitoring and operational logs and the permit before reaching a conclusion.

searches.query: Restronguet Creek Carnon River sewage storm overflow pollution
searches.answer:
The information provided points to **mining pollution, not a sewage overflow**, as the documented pollution problem in Restronguet Creek and the Carnon River.

In 1992, more than 45 million litres of contaminated water escaped from the closed Wheal Jane mine after an adit collapsed. The discharge turned the river reddish and flowed into Restronguet Creek, killing fish. Metal contamination from historic mining has also affected creek sediments and wildlife; a treatment works was later installed to intercept and treat contaminated mine water.

The available sources do **not** identify a sewage storm overflow or provide details about sewage discharges.

objections_refuted: Localised convective rainfall missed by the gauges: two independent gauges both show near-zero rain, the fact-checker found no weather report of rain in the area, and regulators described regional drought and dry weather in early November 2026, so this is now weakly supported at best.
Groundwater infiltration or snow-melt: the area was in drought conditions and temperatures were around 5°C, so there is no support for either.

Pump failure or emergency discharge as an innocent cause: no reported failure was found. Even if one occurred, the 2026 prosecution shows that failing to take remedial measures after a pump failure can itself be an offence, so it would not clear the event for investigation purposes.
objections_standing: EDM sensor fault or telemetry glitch: the event has no end time and a null status, and nothing found either confirms or rules out a monitor or data-feed artefact.
Tidal or back-flow influence: Restronguet Creek is the tidal reach of the river, so this is physically possible, though there is no evidence the outfall sits in the tidal reach.
Gauge distance of 5.7–6.5 km: this is a residual uncertainty without radar confirmation, though no evidence of rain was found.
Permit conditions and the true duration of the event are unknown.
ruling.reasoning: Both gauges recorded at or below 0.2 mm across every window, which is below the commonly cited 0.25 mm dry-spill threshold. The monitor is online, and the spill lasted more than 21 hours. Web evidence points to regional drought and dry weather, which supports the gauge readings. The skeptic's highest-rated explanation, a pump failure, has no supporting evidence and would not excuse the event anyway. The main open caveats are the unclosed event record, which leaves a sensor or telemetry artefact possible, and possible tidal influence, both of which are unverified. This is a credible dry-spill candidate that warrants investigation, but it is not conclusive.

# Evidence pack: possible dry-weather spill, SBB00211 (South West Water, Carnon River)

## Summary

- **Pipeline verdict:** `likely_breach`. Adjudicator confidence is 0.68.
- **The event:** Storm overflow SBB00211 began discharging to the Carnon River at 2026-11-13 17:14:21 UTC. It had run for 21.1 hours with no recorded end when the data was pulled.
- **Rainfall:** Two rain gauges 5.7 km and 6.5 km away recorded at most 0.2 mm in the 48 hours before the spill and 0.0 mm during it.
- **Online evidence:** Searches found no report of a pump failure, power cut or local rain. Regulators described parts of the South West Water region as still in "severe drought" on 5 Nov 2026.
- **Open caveats:** The event record is unclosed (status null, no end time). The gauges are more than 5 km away. A sensor or telemetry fault and tidal influence have not been ruled out.
- **Disagreement between assessments:** The skeptic model put breach confidence at 0.25. Two earlier reviews of this same event reached `likely_innocent` (0.35) and `needs_review` (0.55), neither using external sources.
- **Recommendation:** Refer to the Environment Agency as a **possible** breach for investigation. This is not a confirmed breach.

## The spill (data)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Overflow ID | SBB00211 |
| Company | South West Water |
| Receiving watercourse | Carnon River |
| Location | 50.218504, -5.103782 |

| Status | **null** |
| Duration at data pull | 21.1 h (lower bound, event still open) |
| Monitor offline | false |
| Feed verdict | `dry_spill_candidate` |

## Innocent explanations considered

| Explanation | Skeptic rating | Status after evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Pump failure or power outage causing an emergency discharge | high | **No supporting evidence found.** The search found no reported failure at Devoran, Bissoe or Carnon Downs in Nov 2026. Such failures are often not publicised, so this is not ruled out. A pump failure may not excuse the event: one of the 18 charges in the 2026 prosecution was failing to take remedial measures after a pumping-station failure (https://theintelligent.co.uk/environment/2026/south-west-water-fined-nearly-ps8-million-sewage-spills-across-devon-and-cornwall). |
| Monitor (EDM) sensor fault or false "open" signal | medium | **Standing.** The monitor is reported online, but nothing confirms or rules out an artefact. |
| Telemetry or data-feed error that failed to close the event | medium | **Standing.** The null status and missing end time are consistent with this. |
| Localised rain missed by gauges 5.7–6.5 km away | medium | **Weakened, not eliminated.** Both gauges read near zero, no weather report of rain was found, and the region was described as in drought. There is no radar confirmation. |
| Tide-locking or back-flow | low | **Standing as physically possible.** Restronguet Creek is the tidal part of the river (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restronguet_Creek; https://www.feockparishcouncil.gov.uk/ourcreek). It is unverified whether the outfall sits in the tidal reach. |
| Groundwater infiltration or snow-melt | low | **Unsupported.** This is inconsistent with the drought conditions reported. The ~5°C figure comes only from a forecast widget. |

**Skeptic's strongest objection (verbatim):**
> "The event lacks a confirmed end time and the rain gauges are >5 km from the outfall; such spacing can easily miss localized rain, while sensor or data‑feed glitches can produce a prolonged open signal, making the dry‑spill inference unreliable."

This objection has not been fully answered. The rainfall side is partly addressed by two agreeing gauges and the drought context. The sensor and telemetry side is not addressed at all and can only be resolved with South West Water's own monitoring records.

**Separate point on river pollution:** The Carnon River and Restronguet Creek carry long-standing mine-water metal pollution, including the 1992 Wheal Jane release (https://challenginghabitat.com/2023/10/17/restronguet-creek-revisited/; https://www.feockparishcouncil.gov.uk/ourcreek). This does not explain an overflow monitor signal. However, river colour or water quality should not be used as evidence of sewage here without testing.

The spread is wide. The rise from earlier reviews is driven mainly by the drought context and the absence of any reported operational cause. Neither of these is direct evidence about this outfall.

**Recommendation:** Send as a report of a **possible** breach, asking the Environment Agency to obtain the following.

1. South West Water's EDM record for SBB00211, including the final end time, total duration and any fault or alarm flags.
2. Operational logs for 13–14 Nov 2026, covering pumps, power, blockages and any emergency discharge.
3. The permit conditions for SBB00211, especially the pass-forward flow requirement and the conditions under which spills are allowed.
4. Rainfall radar for 11–14 Nov over the catchment.
5. Whether the outfall is in the tidal reach, and tide levels at the time.
6. Any earlier dry-weather spills at this overflow on other dates.

**Checks for the reviewer before sending:**
- Confirm the 0.25 mm definition against a primary source.
- Do not rely on the Playing Place proximity claim unless verified.
